passage:
The canteen at the training institute was almost empty when Shankar saw the spreadsheet on a shared screen. It was the trainer pay sheet, left open by mistake. Next to Lokesh's name, in the same role, was a figure noticeably higher than his own.

His stomach dropped. His first thought was to walk over to Lokesh and say something sharp.

Instead he went back to his desk and asked himself what he actually knew. It was one sheet, unlabelled. Lokesh had two more years in the job and a professional certificate that Shankar lacked.

That evening he wrote a list: his certifications, the workshops he ran, the feedback scores. The next Monday he asked the head of training for a review, and said, "I'd like to understand how the pay levels are set." He didn't mention Lokesh once.

qa.q: What did Shankar see on the shared screen?
qa.a: Shankar saw the trainer pay sheet, which showed a higher figure next to Lokesh's name for the same role.

qa.q: What was Shankar's first impulse, and what does it show?
qa.a: Shankar's first thought was to say something sharp to Lokesh, showing that he felt hurt and envious at the news.

qa.q: What did Shankar do that was wise?
qa.a: Shankar checked what he actually knew, compared skills and experience, listed evidence and asked the head of training about how pay levels are set without attacking Lokesh.

qa.q: How might Lokesh have felt if Shankar had confronted Lokesh?
qa.a: Lokesh could have felt blindsided and defensive, since the pay decision was not Lokesh's and Lokesh may not have known about the sheet at all.

grounding: Shankar learns a peer earns more for the same role, feels his stomach drop and negotiates with evidence instead of attacking the peer.
